09/ 22.03.2023 Heard Mr. Shashi Kumar Ojha, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner, Mr.
Jitendra Pandey, learned A.P.P. appearing for the State and Mr. Ram Lakhan Yadav, learned counsel appearing for the O.P. No. 2.
2.

This petition has been filed for quashing of the entire criminal proceedings including the order taking cognizance dated 18.12.2012, by which, cognizance for the offences under Sections 420 and 406 of IPC has been taken against the petitioner, in connection with Complaint Case No. 172 of 2011, pending in the court of learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Koderma.
3.

The complaint case was lodged by the O.P. No. 2 stating therein that Bahadur Yadav has lodged the instant complaint case being C- 172/11 in the court of the C.J.M, Kodarma against the petitioner alleging therein that he made an agreement with the petitioner on 10.03.2008 for sale of a Hywa truck bearing Reg. No. LPK 2516 TC/38 E-2 which he has purchased through finance from Tata Motor Finance Ltd.

In view of the terms of aforesaid agreement the petitioner had given Rs.
1,65,000/- by way of maintenance of the vehicle and further required to be paid Rs. 1,00,000/- for finance installment.
The vehicle was handed over to the petitioner for plying it on road.

It was further agreed upon by the parties that the complainant/ vender will liable to cover all the risk of the vehicle till the date of agreement and the purchaser will be liable to pay the dues of the finance but the purchaser/ petitioner has failed to pay the dues of the financer.
Though it is alleged that the petitioner was day to day earning by plying the vehicle.
It is further alleged that the complainant sent a legal notice to the petitioner which was not replied by him.

More so, the petitioner had abused Saheb Mahto vs The State Of Jharkhand on 22 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87834406/
1 the complainant by saying him handicapped and also threatened him with life and refused to pay the dues amount in presence of the witnesses.

sentences.text: 4. Learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submits that pursuant to an agreement dated 10.03.2008, O.P. No. 2 has handed over his hywa vehicle to the petitioner, which was duly signed and agreed by and between the petitioner and the O.P. No. 2 in present of the witnesses.

The payment was made by the petitioner on the strength of the agreement and following thereto the O.P.
No. 2 handed over the vehicle in question to the petitioner on being duly satisfied.

He further submits that the petitioner has gone on paying the amount in terms of the agreement and has already paid a sum of Rs. 1,65,000/-, however, subsequently he has not been able to pay further installment, for that, the complaint case has been filed.

He further submits that no ingredients of Sections 420 and 406 of the Indian Penal Code are made out and only on the basis of complaint and by way of adducing certain enquiry witnesses, the learned court has taken the cognizance for a civil wrong.
On these grounds, he submits that entire proceeding may kindly be quashed.

5. Learned counsel appearing for the O.P. No. 2 submits that admittedly the agreement was there and in view of the agreement, the hywa vehicle was handed over to the petitioner and the petitioner has not paid a sum of Rs. 1 lakh, that's why the complaint case has been filed.
He submits that criminality is made out and this court sitting under Section 482 Cr.P.C., at this stage, may not quash the entire criminal proceeding.
He further submits that it is well settled that if the criminality is made out, civil case and criminal case both can go on simultaneously.
6. Learned A.P.P. appearing for the State submits that the learned court after looking into the SA and the statements of two enquiry witnesses has taken the cognizance.
7. In view of the above submissions of the parties, the court has gone through the contents of the complaint as well as the order taking cognizance.

Admittedly, the case is arising out of an agreement entered into between the petitioner and the O.P. No. 2 and it was agreed that a sum of Rs.
2,65,000/- shall be paid by the petitioner to the O.P. No. 2.
From the draft annexed with the petition, it is crystal clear that a sum of Rs. 1,65,000/- has already been paid by the petitioner and for recovery of Rs. 1 lakh, the complaint case has been filed.
This is not a case that from the very beginning, intention was there to cheat the O.P. No. 2, in light of Section 415 of IPC.

It is well settled that to hold a person guilty, as defined under Section 415 of IPC, it is necessary to show that he had fraudulent or dishonest intention at the time of making a promise and to retain the property.

In view of this definition and considering the fact that the petitioner was going on paying the amount and paid a sum of Rs. 1,65,000/- to the O.P. No. 2, which is the admitted position, it cannot be said that from the very beginning it was the intention of the petitioner to cheat the O.P. No. 2.

Moreover,
the case is arising out of an agreement and it appears that for a civil wrong, criminal case has been filed.

It is well settled that the criminal motion by way of adducing two enquiry witnesses only in absence of the criminality is a very serious matter, as has been held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Pepsi Food Limited and Anr. Versus Special Judicial Magistrate & Others, reported in (1998) (5) SCC 749.

There is no doubt, if the criminality is made out, civil and criminal cases both can go on simultaneously, as has been argued by the learned counsel appearing for the O.P. No. 2,
however, in the case in hand, after considering the definition of cheating under Section 415 IPC, no Saheb Mahto vs The State Of Jharkhand on 22 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87834406/
2 criminality is made out.
8.

sentences.text:
In view of the above facts, reasons and analysis, the entire criminal proceedings including the order taking cognizance dated 18.12.2012, by which, cognizance for the offences under Sections 420 and 406 of IPC has been taken against the petitioner, in connection with Complaint Case No. 172 of 2011, pending in the court of learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Koderma, are hereby, quashed.
9. This petition is allowed and disposed of.
10. It is made clear that if any civil action is brought by the O.P. No. 2, that shall be decided on its own merits without being prejudiced by the order of this Court.

(Sanjay Kumar Dwivedi, J.) Amitesh/-
